Its silhouette must immediately read as Balcony Modern, and the physical assembly must include load-bearing deck or roof surface, wall or column supports, edge beam or fascia, rail, drip edge, or weather boundary, connection brackets, drainage or runoff path, underside and service detail, foundation or structural base, primary load-bearing massing, public entrance or connection face, framed openings, roof or upper termination, service elevation or access, material and weather transitions. Use structural frame, deck or roof finish, rail or fascia material, mounting hardware, dark metal, black composite, tinted glass, cyan, magenta, violet with construction, wear, mounting, and service detail appropriate to techtown. The target envelope is approximately 4 meters wide, 2.2 meters deep, and 1.2 meters high, subject only to reviewed functional protrusions. The blueprint evidence is: 13. Asset families The uploaded asset plan already breaks TechTown into useful asset families. This blueprint keeps that structure and adds town-function requirements. A. Architecture / exteriors Hero exteriors: Modular kit:

Physical identity and semantic decision: the final category is architecture because strong filename prefix resolves the physical object as architecture. Model it as a complete architectural asset with a legible public face, believable side and service elevations, and construction logic appropriate to its use. Words describing an animal, profession, customer, owner, district, collection, or story function may not force character or creature anatomy onto an object such as a cottage, boat, crate, display, station, rack, board, feeder, machine, sign, or piece of equipment. The named object must be identifiable in neutral clay material before labels, color, and glow are applied.

Silhouette and proportion: Establish the building or structural-module category from massing, roof or overhead profile, entrance or connection hierarchy, structural bays, openings, and ground or support relationship before signage and color are visible. Keep the working envelope near 4 meters wide, 2.2 meters deep, and 1.2 meters high. Only reviewed protrusions such as signs, arms, doors, mirrors, roots, branches, railings, hoses, lighting, propulsion, awnings, stairs, or service hardware may extend beyond it. Every major and secondary form must reinforce Balcony Modern; unrelated decorative mass should be removed.

Construction and functional anatomy: Model a coherent foundation, frame or load-bearing wall system, layered facade or structural depth, human-scale access, glazing or openings with frames, weather and drainage treatment, service access, and credible transitions between materials. Required visible components are load-bearing deck or roof surface, wall or column supports, edge beam or fascia, rail, drip edge, or weather boundary, connection brackets, drainage or runoff path, underside and service detail, foundation or structural base, primary load-bearing massing, public entrance or connection face, framed openings, roof or upper termination, service elevation or access, material and weather transitions. Each one must connect through credible frames, joints, seams, foundations, roots, brackets, fasteners, cables, pipes, glazing frames, hinges, biological attachment, serving structure, packaging, or material transitions. Flat paint, decals, and emission may not replace a component that explains operation, weight support, access, occupancy, growth, containment, drainage, power, preparation, protection, or maintenance.

Materials, color, and lighting: use the named material vocabulary dark brushed metal, black composite, tinted glass, controlled emissive accents, dark metal, cyan, magenta, violet, electric blue. sleek cyberpunk smart city; dark brushed metal, black composite panels, tinted glass, polished concrete, controlled cyan, magenta, violet, and electric-blue lighting. Metal surfaces need distinct painted, powder-coated, galvanized, brushed, cast, polished, oxidized, or heat-affected responses rather than one universal gray material. Glass requires thickness, framing, tint appropriate to the town, controlled transparency, believable roughness, and an interior or backing surface so it does not read as an empty blue plane. Stone, brick, concrete, plaster, stucco, tile, and asphalt should show scale-correct joints, aggregate or surface breakup, edge wear, drainage staining, and construction transitions without noisy procedural speckling. Wood needs believable board direction, grain scale, end grain, joinery, sealing, wear, and moisture response appropriate to indoor, residential, marine, fantasy, or industrial use. Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling. Emissive accents must arise from a lens, strip, screen, projector, fixture, biological organ, or energy component. Do not paint unexplained neon lines across ordinary structure. Avoid the town-specific failures: Jetsons retro-future, rounded toy sci-fi, sterile white-only futurism, rainbow neon soup, Roblox block filler. Surface variation should follow manufacturing, age, handling, weather, moisture, heat, pressure, preparation, cleaning, or maintenance rather than random noise. Emissive areas must originate from a real lens, screen, fixture, projector, biological organ, or energy system.

Condition and environmental integration: Keep primary surfaces precision-made and maintained, with restrained use at handles, service fasteners, floor interfaces, vents, charging contacts, propulsion hardware, and controls. Emissive accents originate from real lenses, screens, fixtures, or energy systems and remain controlled. Place it on the parcel, terrain shelf, dock edge, modular foundation, or interior footprint named by the blueprint. Public access faces navigation and social space; service access faces the alley, utility corridor, backstage zone, waterfront service edge, or maintenance route. Foundation, stairs, ramps, porches, piles, retaining walls, and terrain transitions must meet the environment without floating gaps. Add contact shadows, foundations, feet, brackets, roots, piles, seals, trim, drainage, terrain blending, waterline response, or wall transitions where the object meets its environment. It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Interaction and state design: Keep entrances, shutters, gates, windows, awnings, stairs, ramps, elevators, signs, lighting, roof equipment, and service components separable whenever gameplay or state changes may need them. Expected hooks include transform, material-state, damage, pickup, or placement hook only where gameplay requires it. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use modular floor, wall, roof, stair, rail, counter, doorway, foundation, and major structural collision. Walkable areas, entrances, windows used for gameplay, and service openings must match the visible model, while trim, roof equipment, cables, fasteners, and inaccessible facade detail remain simplified or nonblocking. Use positive Z as the principal entrance, public face, or module-forward direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at ground level or the documented connection plane near the footprint center. Use one named asset root, semantically named render meshes, separate animated or stateful parts, simplified collision, and metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, final semantic category, and specification version. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Preserve massing, entrances, openings, supports, and skyline in every LOD. Repeating windows, panels, rails, trim, and structural members should use shared geometry or instancing. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 39,000 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Medium-range output should target roughly 18,000 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights. Far output should target roughly 6,000 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature. Reduction may never destroy this recognition requirement: Establish the building or structural-module category from massing, roof or overhead profile, entrance or connection hierarchy, structural bays, openings, and ground or support relationship before signage and color are visible.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Balcony Modern is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.

Inventory audit: This asset is explicitly listed in a town, ecosystem, travel, or gameplay-system blueprint and belongs in the production specification library. Required action: Generate when its town palette, family builder, dependencies, and quality gates are production-ready.

Silhouette and proportion: Establish the building or structural-module category from massing, roof or overhead profile, entrance or connection hierarchy, structural bays, openings, and ground or support relationship before signage and color are visible. Keep the working envelope near 4 meters wide, 0.45 meters deep, and 3.2 meters high. Only reviewed protrusions such as signs, arms, doors, mirrors, roots, branches, railings, hoses, lighting, propulsion, awnings, stairs, or service hardware may extend beyond it. Every major and secondary form must reinforce Wall Panel Metal; unrelated decorative mass should be removed.

Construction and functional anatomy: Model a coherent foundation, frame or load-bearing wall system, layered facade or structural depth, human-scale access, glazing or openings with frames, weather and drainage treatment, service access, and credible transitions between materials. Required visible components are structural wall panel, base or foundation connection, left and right module edges, top cap, parapet, or roof connection, front finish layers, rear or interior construction face, opening, trim, or utility pass-through where named, foundation or structural base, primary load-bearing massing, public entrance or connection face, framed openings, roof or upper termination, service elevation or access, material and weather transitions. Each one must connect through credible frames, joints, seams, foundations, roots, brackets, fasteners, cables, pipes, glazing frames, hinges, biological attachment, serving structure, packaging, or material transitions. Flat paint, decals, and emission may not replace a component that explains operation, weight support, access, occupancy, growth, containment, drainage, power, preparation, protection, or maintenance.

Materials, color, and lighting: use the named material vocabulary dark brushed metal, black composite, tinted glass, controlled emissive accents, dark metal, cyan, magenta, violet, electric blue. sleek cyberpunk smart city; dark brushed metal, black composite panels, tinted glass, polished concrete, controlled cyan, magenta, violet, and electric-blue lighting. Metal surfaces need distinct painted, powder-coated, galvanized, brushed, cast, polished, oxidized, or heat-affected responses rather than one universal gray material. Glass requires thickness, framing, tint appropriate to the town, controlled transparency, believable roughness, and an interior or backing surface so it does not read as an empty blue plane. Stone, brick, concrete, plaster, stucco, tile, and asphalt should show scale-correct joints, aggregate or surface breakup, edge wear, drainage staining, and construction transitions without noisy procedural speckling. Wood needs believable board direction, grain scale, end grain, joinery, sealing, wear, and moisture response appropriate to indoor, residential, marine, fantasy, or industrial use. Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling. Emissive accents must arise from a lens, strip, screen, projector, fixture, biological organ, or energy component. Do not paint unexplained neon lines across ordinary structure. Avoid the town-specific failures: Jetsons retro-future, rounded toy sci-fi, sterile white-only futurism, rainbow neon soup, Roblox block filler. Surface variation should follow manufacturing, age, handling, weather, moisture, heat, pressure, preparation, cleaning, or maintenance rather than random noise. Emissive areas must originate from a real lens, screen, fixture, projector, biological organ, or energy system.

Condition and environmental integration: Keep primary surfaces precision-made and maintained, with restrained use at handles, service fasteners, floor interfaces, vents, charging contacts, propulsion hardware, and controls. Emissive accents originate from real lenses, screens, fixtures, or energy systems and remain controlled. Place it on the parcel, terrain shelf, dock edge, modular foundation, or interior footprint named by the blueprint. Public access faces navigation and social space; service access faces the alley, utility corridor, backstage zone, waterfront service edge, or maintenance route. Foundation, stairs, ramps, porches, piles, retaining walls, and terrain transitions must meet the environment without floating gaps. Add contact shadows, foundations, feet, brackets, roots, piles, seals, trim, drainage, terrain blending, waterline response, or wall transitions where the object meets its environment. It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Interaction and state design: Keep entrances, shutters, gates, windows, awnings, stairs, ramps, elevators, signs, lighting, roof equipment, and service components separable whenever gameplay or state changes may need them. Expected hooks include transform, material-state, damage, pickup, or placement hook only where gameplay requires it. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use modular floor, wall, roof, stair, rail, counter, doorway, foundation, and major structural collision. Walkable areas, entrances, windows used for gameplay, and service openings must match the visible model, while trim, roof equipment, cables, fasteners, and inaccessible facade detail remain simplified or nonblocking. Use positive Z as the principal entrance, public face, or module-forward direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at ground level or the documented connection plane near the footprint center. Use one named asset root, semantically named render meshes, separate animated or stateful parts, simplified collision, and metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, final semantic category, and specification version. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Preserve massing, entrances, openings, supports, and skyline in every LOD. Repeating windows, panels, rails, trim, and structural members should use shared geometry or instancing. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 39,000 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Medium-range output should target roughly 18,000 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights. Far output should target roughly 6,000 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature. Reduction may never destroy this recognition requirement: Establish the building or structural-module category from massing, roof or overhead profile, entrance or connection hierarchy, structural bays, openings, and ground or support relationship before signage and color are visible.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Wall Panel Metal is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.

No gaps, overlaps, floating ends, or invisible ledges are allowed. Add contact shadows, foundations, feet, brackets, roots, piles, seals, trim, drainage, terrain blending, waterline response, or wall transitions where the object meets its environment. It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Expected hooks include day, night, powered, warning, and damaged light states. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Distant LODs may reduce cracks and hardware but cannot change grade, gaps, width, edge safety, or traversal timing. Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. Backing, supports, power, weather protection, and service access may not disappear into or float away from the mounting surface. Add contact shadows, foundations, feet, brackets, roots, piles, seals, trim, drainage, terrain blending, waterline response, or wall transitions where the object meets its environment. It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Interaction and state design: Keep lettering, logos, display surfaces, indicator lights, changeable panels, and emissive layers separate for localization, state changes, damage, content updates, and nighttime use. Expected hooks include changeable display, content, or emissive state, day, night, powered, warning, and damaged light states. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use one or more primitive or low-complexity hulls matching the major blocking volume and interaction surface. Decorative handles, cables, slats, fasteners, trim, lenses, foliage, and surface detail must not create snagging collision. Use positive Z as the primary viewing face and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at the ground support, wall-mount center, hanging point, or portable base. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Use mesh or texture lettering according to viewing distance. LODs must preserve panel shape, color block, mounting, primary wordmark, and display state without excessive geometry. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 14,040 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Medium-range output should target roughly 6,480 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights. Far output should target roughly 2,160 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature. Reduction may never destroy this recognition requirement: Panel shape, scale, mounting, viewing angle, border or bezel, and support must identify the sign category before text is read. Lettering cannot be the sole distinction.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Small Robot Display is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.
